The previously cited SDD components (hestia/main.py, hestia/api/limiter.py) do not actually implement or bound concurrent-session capacity; api/limiter.py governs only the /login rate limit (docs/icd.md EXT-01), unrelated to this NFR. Requirement: The system's deployment guide shall mandate encrypted storage for all databases and encrypted transport between components, and shall specify the minimum required controls. Operator confirmation of compliance shall be a prerequisite for production deployment.

No deployment guide gate, operator attestation step, or documented minimum-control checklist exists anywhere in README.md, docker-compose.yml, or Dockerfile. This is a direct requirement-vs-documented-state contradiction, not merely an absence of implementation.

Requirement: The system's audit logs shall be tamper-evident and shall support extraction of a complete structured audit record scoped by time window, principal, or resource by an authorised administrator.
Notes: The structured-extraction-scoped-by-time/principal/resource half is satisfied: FC-25/EXT-13 (GET /admin/logs) filters by level/search/since/until and exports NDJSON/CSV. The tamper-evident half is NOT implemented: system.log/audit.log (hestia/infrastructure/logging/config.py) are plain, rotated JSON-line files with standard filesystem permissions only; no hash-chaining, cryptographic signing, append-only/WORM storage, or external log-shipping exists. No SRS or TST covers either half of this requirement explicitly (SRS-027/TST-037/TST-039 cover audit event coverage, not extraction or tamper-evidence).

Requirement: The system shall ensure that access to personal data is restricted to authorised users and processes acting under the controller's authority, and shall ensure that such access is logged and auditable.
Notes: RBAC (FC-02/03/14) restricts access to authorised users/processes and audit logging (FC-18) makes that access auditable; this GDPR obligation is substantively the same claim as MRS-003/MRS-062/MRS-063/MRS-064, which already trace cleanly.

Requirement: The system shall enable the controller to demonstrate compliance with applicable data-protection obligations through documentation and auditable records.

Requirement: The system shall support the controller in fulfilling data-subject rights, including rectification, erasure, and portability, within the processor's scope.

Requirement: The system shall maintain resilience and the capability to restore personal data and processing functions within agreed recovery objectives.
Notes: Directly corresponds to the backup/disaster-recovery gap already identified in docs/sdd.md section 11.4 and its production-readiness review: no backup, snapshot, or restore mechanism exists for users.db, the sparse-corpus files, or Qdrant, and no RTO/RPO is defined anywhere.

Requirement: The system shall record any personal-data breach and notify the controller without undue delay, providing sufficient information for the controller to meet its notification obligations under Art. 33.1 and Art. 34.
